summary: Backend-only test of the email delivery fix (Resend). 6/6 pytest tests passed. A live Resend send to s02329739@gmail.com (the account owner) returned a non-empty id. _deliver_in_background on a seeded paid bookkeeping order set delivery_status='sent' and delivered_to=s02329739@gmail.com. POST /api/checkout/verify was run in-process with razorpay_client mocked (signature check passes, payment.fetch returns the owner email). It returned 200 {status:'paid', delivery:'queued'}, and the background task then saved delivery_status='sent'. The bookkeeping template contains the PDF URL, all 3 spreadsheet/Drive links, the File -> Make a copy steps, '10am to 7pm' and medicalmasterbook@gmail.com, and it passes the email safety checks. The bookkeeping block is absent for other products. The product, combo-6 add-on and settings endpoints return the expected URLs and values.

minor.issue: RESEND_FROM holds the Resend API key instead of an email address. The code falls back to onboarding@resend.dev, so sending works, but emails come from Resend's shared sandbox sender. Once a domain is verified, set RESEND_FROM to something like 'LedgerKit <orders@yourdomain>'.

product_limitation_not_a_bug: Resend sandbox: until a domain is verified at resend.com/domains, Resend only accepts mail to the account owner (s02329739@gmail.com) and rejects other buyers with 403 validation_error. When that happens, send_email returns None and the order is marked delivery_status='pending'. Real customers will not get emails until the user verifies a domain and updates RESEND_FROM. A live send to medicalmasterbook@gmail.com was deliberately not attempted, as instructed.
action_items: Tell the user to verify a sending domain in Resend and set RESEND_FROM to an address on that domain; without this, real buyers will not get emails.
Optional: add an admin re-send endpoint or job for orders with delivery_status='pending', so buyers whose emails failed during the sandbox period can get their products after the domain is verified.
critical_code_review_comments: verify_razorpay_payment passes the pre-update `order` doc to the background task. That works because _deliver_products uses buyer_email separately, but anything that reads order['status'] there would see the stale value.

If verify is called twice before the first background task finishes, two emails can be sent, because delivery_status is only set after the send completes. Consider an atomic 'sending' claim (find_one_and_update) first.
Failed sends are only logged and marked 'pending'. Nothing retries them.
seed_data_creation: TEST_-prefixed orders were inserted in-process and deleted afterwards.
context_for_next_testing_agent: test_email_delivery.py imports server/email_service directly and runs the live Resend and mocked-Razorpay verify flow in one asyncio.run to avoid motor loop issues. It only sends live email to s02329739@gmail.com.
